Facility Inventory & Condition Assessmen.justification: The plan includes an inventory of all district facilities with details on building sizes, ages, and non-classroom spaces such as athletic fields and multipurpose rooms (Section 1, Overview & Process). The condition assessment includes evaluations of building systems and identifies areas for improvement, using more comprehensive tools than FIT, but does not fully integrate real-time monitoring or detailed lifecycle planning.

Enrollment & Capacity Planning.justification: The plan provides a comprehensive enrollment analysis with detailed methodology including demographic trends, housing patterns, and community data (Section 2.2, Analysis of Enrollment Projections). It includes detailed capacity utilization data by site and grade, connects projections to facility actions, and discusses strategies for adapting to declining enrollment.

Educational Alignment.justification: Educational alignment is a core organizing principle, with a comprehensive educational program vision linking district mission and instructional priorities to facilities planning (Section 2.4). The plan details how facilities support multiple programs including TK, special education, and technology integration, with clear connections between projects and educational goals.

Outdoor Spaces & Greening.justification: There is no mention or minimal reference to outdoor spaces or schoolyard greening in the facilities planning sections reviewed.

Climate Risk & Mitigation.justification: The plan does not mention climate risks or climate readiness; no assessment or strategies related to climate impacts are included.

Energy Efficiency & Resilience.justification: No mention or minimal reference to energy efficiency, electrification, decarbonization, or energy resilience was found in the provided content.

Financial Plan & Capital Strategy.justification: The plan includes probable cost estimates and scope prioritization (Section 3), and mentions funding sources such as local revenue and state eligibility, but lacks detailed cost estimating methods, comprehensive financial planning, or prioritization criteria.
